title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and improve cache hygiene
author: Asha Rao
body:
Context: Our CI workflows have accumulated responsibilities over time: lint, unit/test, integration, release automation and cache management. This PR splits the large monolithic CI workflow into focused workflows (lint, test, release) and extracts cache management into a reusable ci-cache workflow. Motivation: improve clarity, reduce incidental rebuilds, speed up common developer flows (lint-only and test-only pushes), and tighten cache key hygiene to avoid stale artifacts causing CI flakes.

What changed (summary):
- Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into three primary workflows: lint-and-static.yml, test.yml, release.yml. The old composite workflow was deprecated.
- Introduced .github/workflows/ci-cache.yml which centralizes cache key generation and restore/save steps. Adds explicit cache priming and a periodic cache-prune job (weekly) implemented in tools/ci/scripts/cache-prune.sh.
- Reworked cache keys to include OS, node-version/python-version, and a package-lock/poetry lock checksum to avoid cross-platform poisoning of caches.
- Updated project-level scripts to make test bootstrapping idempotent: redwood/scripts/run-tests.sh (better env validation) and ci-utils.py (cache helpers).
- Added documentation for CI workflows and troubleshooting in tools/ci/README.md and redwood/docs/ci.md.
- Updated multiple repository SDK workflow files to adopt the new ci-cache workflow (examples and SDKs).

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): split lint and test workflows (Asha Rao)
- feat(ci): add reusable ci-cache workflow and cache helpers (Asha Rao)
- chore(ci): update SDKs and examples to reference ci-cache (Asha Rao)
- docs(ci): add troubleshooting and cache priming notes (Asha Rao)
- fix(ci): tighten cache keys to include lockfile checksum (followup)

Files changed (high level):
- Workflow files: created 3 new top-level workflows and deprecated the monolith.
- CI utilities: new scripts and small refactors to make caching idempotent.
- Docs: CI troubleshooting and runbook additions.
- Sample workflows updated across a few repos to adopt the shared cache workflow.

CI and validation:
- GitHub Actions matrix runs: linux/node:14,16,18 on ubuntu-latest, macOS-latest, and windows-latest for the test matrix.
- Initial run: macOS runners experienced a cache-corruption flake on integration tests (false-positive due to cross-platform cache key collision). Root cause: cache key did not include lockfile checksum and macOS path normalization difference.
- Fix applied: updated cache key to include lockfile checksum and OS token; rerun; all checks passed.
- CI summary: 4/4 checks passed on merge (lint, unit, integration, release dry-run).

Review notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally did not move to composite actions at this time to keep workflow files readable and actionable per repo. Future follow-up could extract a composite action for the cache priming step.
- This PR increases the number of workflow files but makes each run cheaper for common changes (e.g., pushes that only change docs will trigger docs/lint but not the full test matrix).
- The periodic cache-prune job is conservative: it lists keys older than 30 days and keeps a retention window. It runs on a weekly cron; ops can tune frequency.

Release notes: minor developer-facing CI changes; no runtime/user-facing changes. See release_notes for the short blurb.

Related work: ENG-5781 (CI hygiene epic), INF-234 (cache stability).

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main after approvals.

feat(ci): add ci-cache reusable workflow and helpers - 2 commits (ci-cache.yml, cache helpers scripts)
chore(ci): update downstream SDK/example workflows to consume ci-cache - 8 commits (small workflow updates)
fix(ci): include lockfile checksum in cache key to prevent cross-platform poisoning - 1 commit
review_thread: Miguel Santos: Please add a note about cache pruning frequency and safety - responded and added tools/ci/README.md explaining prune logic.
Priya Nair: Can we keep a single source of truth for cache key generation? Suggest a helper - added ci-utils.py and moved key generation there.
Ethan Kim: Observed macOS flake on first run, suspect cache collision - confirmed, patched cache key to include OS+lockfile checksum and reran tests.
Miguel Santos: Approved after CI green and docs added.
Priya Nair: Approved - small nits addressed in follow-up commit (typo in README).
Asha Rao (author): Followed up on comments, added explanatory comments in workflows and link to runbook.
release_notes: Developer-facing: CI workflows split (lint/test/release) for faster feedback loops.
Improved cache hygiene: cache keys now include lockfile checksum and OS token to avoid stale caches.
Added weekly cache-prune job to reduce stale artifact accumulation.
Docs: added CI runbook and troubleshooting notes.
